Experience
Platform Engineer – an online grocery delivery start-up, Riyadh          Mar 2025 – Present
– Moved the ordering backend off three hand-configured virtual machines: packaged each service as an image and now run them all on a managed cluster (EKS). Releases went from once a fortnight to several a day.
– Wrote the deployment manifests and the rules that add pods when the evening rush starts and remove them after midnight.
– Every part of the environment (networks, databases, queues) is now described in Terraform files kept in the repository and created by a pipeline, not by clicking in the console. A fresh staging copy takes 20 minutes.
– Built the release pipeline in GitHub Actions: tests, image build, security scan, then a gradual rollout that reverses itself when the error rate climbs.
– After an outage on a Ramadan evening, put dashboards and on-call alerts in place (Grafana on top of Prometheus). The time it takes us to notice a fault fell from about 25 minutes to under 3.
– Split the single flat network into public and private subnets across two availability zones behind a load balancer, with the database reachable only from the application tier.
– Cut the monthly AWS bill by 31% by right-sizing instances and moving product images to a cheaper storage tier.
– Wrote small shell scripts for the nightly database dumps and for log rotation.
